summary: This bill requires the Department of Energy, specified Interior Department bureaus, and FERC to amend all existing covered energy regulations to expire within one year and all new ones to expire within five years, unless the agency extends them for up to five years after public comment and a determination that extension is warranted.

The bill requires covered energy and land-management agencies (DOE, BLM, BOEM, BSEE, OSMRE, FERC) to impose automatic sunset dates on regulations issued under major energy and environmental statutes. Existing rules must expire within one year and new rules within five years unless affirmatively extended after public comment. This mechanism is explicitly intended to reduce regulatory burdens on energy production and therefore limits environmental regulations.
